title: Spinnet requested Host operations (proposal)
description: PROPOSAL ONLY (#70). Not part of Plugin API Level 1, of any stable Level, or of any published Candidate Contract revision; no Host implements it. A Plugin declaring the placeholder candidate host_operations may answer a gesture with one requested Host operation, which the Host commits with the rest of the answer and performs after the script's invocation ends. Besides these shapes the Host checks what a shape cannot say: only an answer to a gesture (the Action's start or an explicit call, submitted, action_chosen) may carry an operation, the requesting Command declares and holds the operation's Capability, inserted text is at most 128 KiB of UTF-8, and the declared candidate revision includes the kind. An answer that breaks a shape or the gesture rule is a protocol violation and ends the View Session; a refused Capability refuses the whole answer and keeps the last good view and state. Definitions under illustrative are not proposed by this revision; they show the generic members holding for mutating kinds owned by other tickets.

operation_id.description: A Plugin-chosen label echoed in operation_finished, never interpreted by the Host: not blank, at most 64 characters.

operation.description: One requested Host operation. kind selects the operation; id, closes_view and notify are common to every kind. closes_view closes the view once the operation succeeds and only then, so a refusal keeps the view to show why. notify asks for an operation_finished View Event when the outcome is ready, delivered only while the session exists and the requesting Action still handles it.

insert_text_operation.description: Inserts text into the App frontmost at execution, through that App's focused element, in place of its selection, by Accessibility only: never the clipboard, never a paste. The Host refuses without writing when the App in front is not the one it showed when the user acted (target_changed), when the view showed no target (target_not_shown), when Spinnet or no App is in front (no_target), or when the App has no element that accepts the text. Needs insert_into_focused_app and Accessibility. No Host confirmation.

text.description: At most 128 KiB of UTF-8, checked by the Host. Empty text is allowed and replaces the selection with nothing, as the Level 1 service does.

view_additions.description: Members a candidate view may carry besides those of its view schema (Level 1's plugin-view.schema.json view today; the new UI contract's view once it exists). shows_insertion_target asks the Host to draw a target line naming the App insertion would go to now, which the Host keeps current and never reveals to the Plugin. A view without it may still insert through a standard insert_text action, whose button carries the target itself; an answer-requested or synchronous insertion from a gesture made in a view that showed no target is refused with target_not_shown.

answer.description: A candidate script's answer: Level 1's answer plus an optional operation. An operation may come with a view, a toast, both or neither, but not with close: an operation that should close the view says closes_view.

view.description: A view, as its view schema describes it, optionally with view_additions.

state.description: Any JSON, at most 64 KiB; null when absent.

allOf.description: An answer that closes the view describes none and requests nothing; use closes_view on the operation instead.
Only an answer with a view keeps a state.

outcome.description: The one terminal result of a request. succeeded: the effect completed as the kind defines. refused: a check at execution failed and nothing was done. declined: the user declined the Host confirmation or closed the view while it was shown. expired: a confirmation went unanswered past its expiry. cancelled: the user cancelled an execution the kind lets them cancel. failed: the effect itself failed after the Host began it.

reason.description: Why a request was refused or failed. Provisional: the insertion reasons wait on the Accessibility evidence of #69. No reason names the App, its bundle ID, process or window.

operation_finished.description: Delivered as the event global when an operation that asked to notify reaches its outcome, while its session exists and the requesting Action still handles it. It runs before any gesture that waited for the operation, behind other earlier events, with the four-second deadline, and is not a gesture: its answer may update the view and state but carries no operation. operation echoes the request's id when it had one.

allOf.description: A refusal or failure says why; no other outcome carries a reason.

event.description: A candidate script's event global: a Level 1 View Event or operation_finished. Gestures, which alone may be answered with an operation, are the Action's start (event null), submitted and action_chosen.

failure_category_additions.description: Action failure categories this candidate would add. insertion_target_changed: a synchronous insert_text inside a View Session found a different App in front than the one the Host showed when the user acted; nothing was inserted, the invocation fails as a refused Host Service does, and the hint updates. Whether this is a category or a message under host_service_failed is product choice P10.

illustrative.description: NOT PROPOSED. Sketches of mutating kinds owned by other tickets (#83 for App exit, the reviewed-task tickets for task start), kept here only to check that the generic members hold. Their names, members, confirmation policies and Capabilities are decided by those tickets.

quit_app_operation.description: Asks the working App to quit, or force-quits it. The Host resolves the target (the App frontmost when the user acted), re-validates its identity at execution, and never names it to the Plugin. Force Quit requires a Host confirmation.

start_task_operation.description: Starts one operation of a reviewed tool profile as a Host-owned task (ADR 0017). Always confirmed by the Host with its own description of the operation and its source. Success means the task started; its completion is reported through the task's own channel, not this request.

start_task_finished.description: operation_finished for a started task may carry an opaque task handle the Plugin can later name to the task's own services.
